projects.title: Mathematical reasoning & AI evaluation
projects.role: Team Lead, Frontier Mathematics; AI Mathematics Expert
projects.summary: Evaluation standards, proof adjudication, and leadership of a 190-person team of IMO medalists.
contribution: I led a 190-person team of IMO medalists, with 8 direct reports, on a multimillion-dollar frontier AI mathematics research project for leading AI labs.
I developed evaluation standards for novel, frontier-level mathematics problems and served as the lead reviewer for ambiguous proofs and model-generated reasoning.
projects.challenge: The work involved deciding whether ambiguous proofs and model-generated arguments were mathematically sound. The evaluation standards had to support research-grade correctness.
projects.outcome: My contributions were the evaluation standards, proof adjudication, and coordination of a large specialist team.
projects.scope: Mercor: August 2025–July 2026. Team Lead, Frontier Mathematics: August 2025–March 2026.
projects.home_summary: I led a 190-person team of IMO medalists, with 8 direct reports. I developed evaluation standards and reviewed ambiguous proofs and model-generated reasoning for mathematical correctness.

projects.title: Crypto forecasting & backtesting
projects.summary: An eight-asset forecasting and backtesting framework with chronological validation and transaction costs.
contribution: I built a cryptocurrency forecasting and backtesting framework across eight assets, using PyTorch LSTMs, logistic regression, and constrained mean-variance optimization.
I separated training, validation, and testing chronologically and evaluated strategies out of sample after transaction costs. The reports include Sharpe, Sortino, Calmar, and drawdown metrics.
projects.challengeTitle: Keeping the test out of sample
projects.challenge: I used chronological splits to separate fitting, model selection, and final evaluation. Scalers are fitted on training observations. Hyperparameters and decision thresholds are chosen on validation data. Position changes incur fees and slippage.
projects.outcome: In the reference test, the LSTM had a smaller maximum drawdown than BTC buy-and-hold, but lower return and Sharpe. This is one test regime; it does not establish consistent outperformance.
projects.scope: Dataset: 1,461 daily observations, downloaded September 3, 2026. Reference test: August 2024–July 2025. One-way fees plus slippage: 15 basis points.
projects.limitations: Daily close-to-close data and a single market regime limit the conclusions. Short borrow costs, market impact, funding rates, and tax effects are not modeled. Eight assets introduce universe-selection risk.
projects.home_summary: I built an eight-asset research framework with LSTMs, logistic regression, portfolio optimization, and transaction costs. The reference test reduced drawdown with the LSTM, but did not beat Bitcoin buy-and-hold on return or Sharpe.

projects.title: Computing on encrypted data
projects.summary: A Legendre-symbol-based partially homomorphic encryption prototype in Python and SageMath.
contribution: I designed and prototyped a Legendre-symbol-based partially homomorphic encryption scheme in Python and SageMath for computation on encrypted healthcare data.
I joined at 14 as one of three selected high-school researchers. During the three-year internship, I studied graduate-level cryptography and worked with senior cryptographers.
projects.challengeTitle: From a cryptographic idea to a prototype
projects.challenge: The research question was how to support computation on encrypted healthcare data with a partially homomorphic encryption scheme. My work connected the mathematical construction to a working prototype.
projects.outcome: I built a research prototype in Python and SageMath.
projects.scope: National Research Institute of Electronics and Cryptology, Kocaeli, Türkiye. September 2022–June 2025.
projects.home_summary: I designed and prototyped a Legendre-symbol-based partially homomorphic encryption scheme in Python and SageMath, for computation on encrypted healthcare data.

projects.title: Leva Math Camp
projects.summary: Co-organizing a national olympiad mathematics program, selecting students, and teaching advanced mathematics.
contribution: I co-led a national olympiad mathematics program, helped select students, and delivered more than 50 advanced lectures. The program selected and trained over 200 students from more than 5,000 applicants, an approximately 4% selection rate.
projects.challenge: My role combined co-organizing the program, selecting students from a national applicant pool, and teaching advanced olympiad mathematics.
projects.outcome: Our program selected and trained more than 200 students. I shared the organizing responsibility and delivered more than 50 advanced lectures.
projects.scope: Türkiye, 2023–2025. Program-level student and applicant counts; shared organizing responsibility.
projects.home_summary: I co-organized a national olympiad math program and gave 50+ advanced lectures. Together, we selected and trained 200+ students from 5,000+ applicants.

projects.title: Reinforcement learning & the Four Color Theorem
projects.summary: Investigating a two-player game formulation of D-reducibility and simpler proof certificates.
contribution: I'm doing research under Prof. Olga Holtz, working with Marco David and Dan Romik on reinforcement learning for the Four Color Theorem.
I'm investigating a two-player game formulation of D-reducibility to understand the structure of computer-assisted proofs and explore simpler proof certificates using machine learning.
projects.challenge: Can a two-player game formulation of D-reducibility help uncover structure in computer-assisted proofs and support simpler proof certificates?
projects.outcome: This work is ongoing. I started in September 2026.
projects.scope: UC Berkeley. Research in progress; this page describes the question being investigated.
projects.home_summary: I'm investigating a two-player game formulation of D-reducibility and the possibility of simpler proof certificates, under Prof. Olga Holtz and working with Marco David and Dan Romik. This is ongoing research.

home.opening: Hi! I'm Ege, an undergrad studying Applied Mathematics and Computer Science at UC Berkeley. I'm particularly interested in AI for math, reasoning, and evaluating coding agents.
home.current: I'm working on reinforcement learning and graph coloring with Prof. Olga Holtz at Berkeley. Previously, I worked on mathematical AI evaluation at Mercor and cryptography at TÜBİTAK BİLGEM.
home.personal: Outside of that, I'm into table tennis, drumming, and working out. I'd love to meet others working on similar topics, discuss research ideas, or work on something together.
home.research_intro: My work has involved checking mathematical reasoning, computing on encrypted data, and using machine learning to study proofs.
